newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says investigates steel dumping.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says investigates steel dumping.

text.p: Thailand is investigating allegations by battered domestic steel producers that Polish and Russian steelmakers are dumping their product in the Thai market, a senior Commerce Ministry official said on Monday.

"We have already sent questionnaires to Poland and Russia to ask them about their market and export prices," Thawatchai Sophastienphong, deputy director-general of the ministry's department of business economics, told Reuters.

In August, representatives from Siam Yamato Steel , a producer of structural steel, and Sahaviriya Steel Industries Plc, which makes hot-rolled coil and steel sheets, asked the Commerce Ministry to investigate the alleged dumping, in which countries price their exports below the local market.
They claimed that imports were sold below the prices in some exporting countries from last year.
Siam Yamato is a subsidiary of Thailand's giant conglomerate Siam Cement Plc.

According to World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules, Thailand must prove the dumping actually took place and that it has had a negative impact on Thai steelmakers before anti-dumping duties can be imposed.
The WTO also requires accused countries to reply to the charges within 30 days. Thawatchai said Poland has asked for an extension but did not say when the complaint was lodged.
Thailand imports steel mainly from Russia, Japan, China and Poland.
The companies said Polish structural steel cost about US$500 per tonne in Poland but only $265 per tonne when exported to Thailand.

"The cheap imports seem to have hurt the local industry tremendously," Thawatchai said. "Steel companies suffered losses from low market prices and high inventories. We are convinced that their complaints are solid enough to warrant investigation," he added.

Sahaviriya Steel Industries was expected to continue to register losses in the third quarter after reporting a loss in the second quarter, battered by depressed prices of global and domestic hot-rolled coil, analysts said.
Thawatchai declined to speculate how long the investigation process would take. The WTO limits such investigations to 18 months.
